proposals.before: Ma Congyun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was dismissed after being sued for seizing the property of his granddaughter, the Huo family heiress.
proposals.after: Ma Congyun, Director of the Palace Secretariat, was dismissed after being sued for embezzling the property of his maternal granddaughter née Huo.
proposals.reason: Chinese 外孫女霍氏 means maternal granddaughter née Huo; idiomatic invents 'Huo family heiress' and drops maternal (外) kinship.

proposals.before: On day xinchou, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting Eastern Capital regent, and Hanlin academician Wang Pu was made deputy regent.
proposals.after: On day xinchou, the Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat Xiang Xun was made acting Eastern Capital regent, and the Academician of Duanming Hall Wang Pu was made deputy regent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 端明殿學士 is Academician of Duanming Hall, not Hanlin academician.

proposals.before: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang records that during Shizong's personal campaign, at Yuzhen he heard Qian's army had pulled back and expected Zhou forces to pursue. He sent Li Chongjin urgently to Zhengyang with the order: "The enemy is coming—attack at once."
proposals.after: (Ma Ling's History of Southern Tang records that during Shizong's personal campaign, at Yuzhen he heard Qian's army had pulled back and expected Tang troops to pursue. He sent Li Chongjin urgently to Zhengyang with the order: "Tang troops are about to arrive; attack them at once."
proposals.reason: Chinese 意唐兵必追之 means he expected Tang troops would pursue, not Zhou forces; idiomatic reverses the referent.

proposals.before: On day dinghai, Xu Xiang, commissioner of the Left Divine Guard Army inside Shouzhou city, and eighteen others came over to the Zhou side.
proposals.after: On day dinghai, Xu Xiang, commissioner of the Left Divine Guard Army inside Shouzhou city, and seventeen others—eighteen in all—came over to the Zhou side.
proposals.reason: Chinese 徐象等一十八人 means Xu Xiang and company totaling eighteen people; literal 'eighteen others' overcounts.

proposals.before: In the third month, on bingshen, acting Guangzhou prefect Chao Chao reported that the enemy director Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon made prefect of Jizhou.
proposals.after: In the third month, on bingshen, acting Guangzhou prefect He Chao reported that the enemy director Zhang Chenghan had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon made prefect of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 何超 is He Chao; idiomatic wrongly doubles the given name as Chao Chao and drops the surname He.

proposals.before: In the third month, on day bingshen, the acting prefect of Guangzhou Chao Chao memorialized that the false-appointed director Zhang Chenghan of Guangzhou had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon appointed prefect of Jizhou.
proposals.after: In the third month, on day bingshen, the acting prefect of Guangzhou He Chao memorialized that the false-appointed director Zhang Chenghan of Guangzhou had surrendered the city; Chenghan was soon appointed prefect of Jizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 何超 is He Chao; literal also mistranslates the name as Chao Chao.

proposals.before: Since Tang lost the Mandate the realm has known sixty years of turmoil—from the catastrophes of Huang Chao and Cai Jing through the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong. The empire was carved among rival warlords, each ruling his own domain, allying with barbarian powers and pressing the central state whenever weakness appeared.
proposals.after: Since Tang lost the Mandate the realm has known sixty years of turmoil—from the catastrophes of Huang Chao and Cai through the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong. The empire was carved among rival warlords, each ruling his own domain, allying with barbarian powers and pressing the central state whenever weakness appeared.
proposals.reason: Chinese 巢、蔡 pairs Huang Chao with Cai (often the Cai-prefecture rebels); idiomatic invents the unsupported personal name Cai Jing.

proposals.before: On bingzi Wang Shenqi, Prince of Chen and governor of Xiangzhou, was promoted to Grand Mentor.
proposals.after: On bingzi An Shenqi, Prince of Chen and governor of Xiangzhou, was promoted to Grand Mentor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 安審琦 is An Shenqi; idiomatic wrongly uses the surname Wang.

proposals.before: On xinyou Xuzhou governor Han Tong was also made chief commandant of the palace horse and foot armies.
proposals.after: On xinyou Xu prefecture governor Han Tong was also made chief commandant of the palace horse and foot armies.
proposals.reason: Chinese 許州 is Xu prefecture (modern Xuchang area), not 徐州; idiomatic conflates the two Xuzhou readings.

decisions.reason: 外孫女 is specifically a daughter's daughter, and 霍氏 identifies her by the Huo surname; the existing idiomatic wording both loses the maternal relationship and invents heiress status.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 幹沒外孫女霍氏之資產

decisions.reason: 端明殿學士 is Academician of Duanming Hall, not a Hanlin academician.
唐兵 is the subject of 必追之, so the original idiomatic field reverses which army Shizong expected to pursue Qian's withdrawing force.
徐象等一十八人 gives a total of eighteen including Xu Xiang, not Xu plus eighteen others.
The official's full name is 何超, He Chao; Chao Chao duplicates the given name and omits the surname.
The paired literal field contains the same duplicated-name error for 何超 and must also use He Chao.

decisions.after: Since Tang lost the Mandate the realm has known sixty years of turmoil—from the catastrophes of Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan through the wars of Zhu Wen and Li Keyong. The empire was carved among rival warlords, each ruling his own domain, allying with barbarian powers and pressing the central state whenever weakness appeared.
decisions.reason: Cai Jing is unsupported, while leaving bare 'Cai' obscurely transliterates the metonym. In this established pairing 蔡 denotes Qin Zongquan and his Caizhou rebels; the same history explicitly writes 蔡賊秦宗權.
The source explicitly gives 安審琦, An Shenqi; Wang Shenqi is a different person who appears earlier in the chapter.

decisions.after: On xinyou, Han Tong, military governor of Xu Prefecture, was also made chief commandant of the palace horse and foot armies.
decisions.reason: 許州 is Xu Prefecture, distinct from 徐州, and the revised wording also preserves the military-governor office expressed by 節度使.

claimRevisions.reason: The source metonym 蔡 identifies Qin Zongquan's Caizhou rebel power, not Cai Jing.
The old interval followed Huang Chao's uprising. Qin Zongquan's independent Caizhou rebellion belongs to AD 884-889.
The structured personal name must agree with 安審琦 and the corrected English prose.
